name: A1308LLHLT-1-T
title: A1308 and A1309 ratiometric linear Hall-effect sensors with analog output
summary: The A1308 and A1309 are linear Hall-effect sensor ICs run from 5 V whose output voltage tracks the magnetic flux density through the die, centred on half the supply with no field present. Sensitivity runs from 0.5 to 9 mV/G by part number, and both the zero-field output and the sensitivity, along with their temperature coefficients, are trimmed in nonvolatile memory at the factory. A chopper-stabilised front end keeps offset drift low; the output is clamped short of both rails, and an undervoltage lockout holds it low until the supply is good. Parts come in a 3-pin SOT-23W (LH) for surface mount and a 3-pin SIP (UA) for through-hole, with the L temperature range reaching 150 °C.

circuits.title: Typical application circuit
circuits.description: The sensor runs from a 5 V supply with a 0.1 µF capacitor across VCC and GND. VOUT drives the output terminal, loaded by RL and a 4.7 nF capacitor, both to ground. The load resistance is 4.7 kΩ minimum and the load capacitance 10 nF maximum.

operation.text: With no field the output sits near half the supply (2.5 V typ at 5 V) and moves up or down with the strength and polarity of the field. The zero-field output, the sensitivity and both clamp levels are proportional to VCC: a supply change of some percentage moves each of them by the same percentage, and the ratiometry errors are the difference between the two changes.
Forward parts raise VOUT in a positive (south-pole) field; the A1309LLHLX-RP9-T is a reverse part, with a sensitivity of –9 mV/G.

Sensitivity, quiescent output and the temperature coefficients of both are set in nonvolatile memory at the end of production. TCSens is programmed at 150 °C for L-range parts and 125 °C for K-range parts, taken against the 25 °C sensitivity.

One BiCMOS die carries the Hall element, temperature compensation for the element's sensitivity drift, a high-gain small-signal amplifier, dynamic offset cancellation, a tuned filter and a low-impedance output stage with clamps. An external bypass capacitor sits on VCC.

The Hall signal is modulated with a high-frequency clock so the field signal and the element's DC offset sit at different frequencies. Demodulation by sample-and-hold returns the field signal to baseband and pushes the offset up in frequency, where an anti-aliasing low-pass and a tuned filter remove it. This removes offset from thermal and mechanical stress, cuts thermal noise and keeps the quiescent output steady after temperature cycling. The chopping frequency is 400 kHz typ.

VOUT is held at GND until VCC climbs above VUVLOHI (3 V max); then it runs as a ratiometric output. If VCC falls below VUVLOLO (2.5 V min) VOUT is pulled low again and stays there until VCC passes VUVLOHI once more. The gap between the two thresholds is hysteresis that prevents an undefined output.
tPO is measured from the moment the supply reaches its minimum operating voltage until the output, under an applied field, settles within ±10% of its final value: 50 µs typ.

A large field step can drive the output past its clamp level briefly. tCLP is the time from the output first reaching the steady clamp voltage until it settles within 1% of it: 30 µs typ with a 10 nF load.

tVCC is the time for VCC to rise from 0 V to its 5 V typical value, from 5 µs to 100 ms. Where VCC is switched on and off (through a multiplexer, for one), the off level must fall to 0.55 V or less for the part to start up correctly next time.

The output stops at VCLPHIGH (4.5 V typ) and VCLPLOW (0.55 V typ). The clamps set the largest positive and negative fields over which the output is linear, and they give the part short-circuit diagnostic capability.
The output has a 3 Ω typical DC resistance and is specified into at least 4.7 kΩ and at most 10 nF to ground. It can source 2 mA and sink 10 mA at most.

LH is a 3-pin SOT-23W (about 2 × 3 × 1 mm) for surface mount; UA is a 3-pin ultramini SIP (about 1.5 × 4 × 3 mm) for through-hole. Both are lead-free with matte-tin plated leadframes. The Hall element sits 0.28 ±0.04 mm below the branded face in the LH and 0.50 ±0.08 mm in the UA.
